soundness_flags.label: Proposition linear-special-case
soundness_flags.one_line: Affineness makes the actual Taylor remainder zero, but the stated certificate and frontier still retain the declared possibly positive L term, so h=d^{-1/2} does not yield the claimed sqrt(d/n) rate unless the proposition explicitly resets the known radius to L=0 or replaces the radius by the affine sharp value.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The journal article studies graphon-drawn interference graphs, defines finite indirect effects and their derivative approximation, and gives a sqrt(rho_n)-scale PC-balancing Gaussian limit under a low-rank sparse-graph regime.
The paper defines an average indirect effect under interference and proves that, in Bernoulli trials, average direct plus indirect effects equal the infinitesimal policy effect.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Sections 2–3, especially the honest-CI discussion and local-polynomial application
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops honest intervals that incorporate worst-case smoothness bias and analyzes bandwidth choice for nonparametric local-polynomial estimators.
The paper develops between-class and ordered-modulus arguments for honest confidence-interval expected length and adaptive procedures.
The paper proves entrywise first-order eigenvector approximations for low-expected-rank random matrices; it does not analyze treatment-weighted exact-support causal scores.

The preprint provides two-to-infinity eigenvector error bounds, row-wise normal approximations, graphon entrywise inference, and a rank-adaptive latent-position equality test; it does not state the proposed causal-score result.
The paper concerns causal inference under approximate neighborhood interference, a locality-based framework distinct from the sparse graphon PC-balancing derivative target.
